confirmed.title: Dark mode: the focus outline on the divider tabs (desktop and mobile) is #1c1b19 drawn on the dark desk, so it can barely be seen (about 1.05:1)
confirmed.expected: README 'Keyboard focus: add a visible outline:2px solid #1c1b19; outline-offset:2px'. The site already treats controls that sit on the desk differently in dark mode: Desk.module.css:18-20 switches the header controls' outline to var(--desk-ink-dark) because a #1c1b19 ring does not show on the dark desk. The divider tabs also sit on the desk. The desktop tabs stick out past the right edge of the paper, and the mobile row sits above the pile. So in dark mode they need an outline that can be seen, just like the header controls.
confirmed.actual: The dark override is limited to `.header :focus-visible`. Tab buttons (Tabs.module.css .tab at line 9 and .tabMobile) fall back to the global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink) }` rule (globals.css:113), which gives rgb(28,27,25) in dark mode. Because of the 2px offset, the ring is drawn on the desk and not on the tab's own coloured background. In dark mode a keyboard user cannot see which tab has focus.
confirmed.evidence: Live build, colorScheme 'dark', /#crumbify at 1440px. Tabbing to each desktop tab gives outlineColor 'rgb(28, 27, 25)' for all five. The header link and toggle give 'rgb(232, 228, 220)'. Pixels sampled from focus-tab-dark-desktop.png: outline pixels 28,27,25 against the desk next to them at 31,29,26, a contrast of about 1.05:1. At 390px (mobile row, focus on 'video bot'), the outline is 28,27,25 against the desk at 38,36,32, about 1.1:1. The screenshots show no visible ring (scratchpad review-r6/behaviour-a11y-responsive/focus-tab-dark-desktop.png and focus-tab-dark-mobile.png). In light mode the same ring sits on #d3ccbf and is clearly visible.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In Tabs.module.css add `:global([data-desk='dark']) .tabsDesktop :focus-visible, :global([data-desk='dark']) .tabsMobile :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--desk-ink-dark); }`. This follows the Desk.module.css:18 pattern. Add an e2e test that, in dark mode, focuses a desktop tab at 1440px and a mobile tab at 390px and asserts outlineColor is rgb(232, 228, 220).
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the live build (port 5204, colorScheme dark, data-desk='dark'). Focusing the desktop 'racing' tab at 1440px and the mobile 'racing' tab at 390px both give outlineColor rgb(28, 27, 25), 2px. The dark override exists only for the desk header (Desk.module.css:18-20 `:global([data-desk='dark']) .header :focus-visible`). Tabs.module.css (.tab line 9, .tabMobile line 68) has no dark rule, so the global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink) }` (globals.css:113-116) applies. With the 2px offset, the ring is drawn on the near-black desk. A screenshot crop of the focused desktop tab shows no visible ring. That breaks gl-24/bh-12 ('visible outline') for the tabs in dark mode. Owner decisions only cover paper controls keeping #1c1b19, and the tabs sit on the desk, not on paper.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Tabs.module.css add: `:global([data-desk='dark']) .tabsDesktop :focus-visible, :global([data-desk='dark']) .tabsMobile :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--desk-ink-dark); }` (mirroring Desk.module.css:18). Add an e2e test in dark mode that focuses a desktop tab at 1440px and a mobile tab at 390px and expects outlineColor rgb(232, 228, 220).

confirmed.title: Reduced motion: bring() still smooth-scrolls to the top, because the JS forces behavior:'smooth' and so overrides the reduced-motion CSS
confirmed.expected: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, globals.css:84-88 sets `html { scroll-behavior: auto }` so the page does not scroll with an animation. bh-13/README: under reduced motion, swaps are instant (the slide is replaced by a cross-fade). The scroll-to-top that bring() performs when scrollY > 80 should therefore jump, not animate.
confirmed.actual: useBring calls `window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })` without checking the preference. An explicit `behavior: 'smooth'` overrides the CSS scroll-behavior, so under reduced motion the page still scrolls with an animation of about 300ms.
confirmed.evidence: Live build, reducedMotion 'reduce', 1440x900. After scrollTo(0,400) I clicked the 'about' tab. scrollY was 388 at +50ms and 0 at +650ms, so the scroll animated rather than jumping to 0. For comparison, without reduced motion the same scroll sampled every 80ms went 318, 96, 10, 0.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In useBring, use `behavior: reducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth'` (reducedMotion is already a parameter of useBring). Extend the bh-04 unit test to assert behavior 'auto' when reducedMotion is true.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: src/lib/usePile.ts:164 calls `window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })` without a reduced-motion check, even though reducedMotion is a parameter of useBring. An explicit behavior:'smooth' overrides the reduced-motion CSS in globals.css:84-88 (`html { scroll-behavior: auto }`). Live test with reducedMotion 'reduce' at 1440x900 on /#cv: scrollTo(0,400), then clicking the 'about' tab, sampled every ~40ms, gave scrollY 400,318,96,42,16,1,0. That is an animated scroll, not a jump. bh-04 prescribes smooth scrolling for the normal case, but bh-13 and the site's own reduced-motion CSS say motion should be removed under reduce.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/usePile.ts:164 change to `window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: reducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth' });`. Extend the bh-04 unit test in usePile.test so that with reducedMotion=true it asserts scrollTo is called with behavior 'auto'.

confirmed.title: From 560 to 640px wide, the sticky note covers part of the CV's 'github.com/AliBars19' contact link and takes clicks on that part
confirmed.expected: The sticky note is a non-interactive hint (atn-27). Content must not be hidden (bh-17). The implementation-notes deviation accepts the note overlapping only 'part of the CV name/tagline' at narrow widths, not a contact link.
confirmed.actual: The note stays interactive to the pointer (it has no pointer-events:none). At viewport widths of about 560 to 640px, its rotated bottom-left corner sits over the right part of the 'github.com/AliBars19' link in the CV contact row. The text 'AliBars19' is visually hidden under the note, and elementFromPoint over that part returns the note instead of the link.
confirmed.evidence: Live build, /#cv. Hit-test over the link's rect, counting points that resolve to the note (DIV.StickyNote_note): 560px 45 points (about 24% of the link, link rect 387-500 x 221-237, note bbox 298-516 x 100-230); 580px 23; 600px 32; 620px 12; 640px 1; 540px 0. The screenshot at 560px (scratchpad review-r6/behaviour-a11y-responsive/note-560.png) shows the note's corner over 'AliBars19'. No other CV control is covered at 320, 360, 390, 430, 480, 520, 599, 700, 768, 1024 or 1440px.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add `pointer-events: none;` to .note in StickyNote.module.css. The note has no click handler (atn-27), so this changes nothing else, and the link stays clickable along its whole length. If the visual overlap also needs fixing, log it as an accepted deviation next to the existing name/tagline note in implementation-notes.md.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced live on /#cv (first load, before any navigation, so the note is shown). Hit-testing the 'github.com/AliBars19' link rect on a 4px grid, the number of points that resolve to the StickyNote div was: 540px 0/112; 560px 37/112 (link rect x 387-500, y 221-237); 580px 20; 600px 27; 620px 12. The 560px screenshot shows the note's rotated bottom-left corner covering the 'AliBars19' part of the link text. StickyNote.module.css .note (line 12) has no pointer-events:none, so the note also takes the clicks. The implementation-notes accepted deviation only covers the note overlapping the CV name/tagline, not a contact link. Impact is limited: the left part of the link still works, and the note disappears after the first navigation (touched). Low severity.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/StickyNote.module.css add `pointer-events: none;` to .note. That is consistent with atn-27, since the note has no handler. To also stop it covering the text, either log the 560-640px overlap as an accepted deviation in docs/implementation-notes.md next to the name/tagline note, or add a media query for (min-width:600px) and (max-width:640px) plus the 560-599 mobile band that moves the note clear (e.g. a smaller `top`/`right` offset). Add an e2e test at 560px that asserts elementFromPoint over the right end of the GitHub link returns the link.

confirmed.title: The comment in the reduced-motion cross-fade e2e test names the wrong sheet: it says it samples 'about' but measures #sheet-crumbify
confirmed.expected: The comment describes what the test does. The test clicks the 'crumbify' tab and reads the opacity of `#sheet-crumbify` (lines 481-487).
confirmed.actual: Line 484 reads `// Sample "about" 50ms after the click, mid-way through the 0.2s`. No 'about' sheet is involved in this test. The comment looks left over from an earlier version and now points a reader at the wrong element.
confirmed.evidence: e2e/pile.spec.ts:481 `const incoming = page.locator('#sheet-crumbify');`, :483 `getByRole('button', { name: 'crumbify' }).click()`, :484 `// Sample "about" 50ms after the click`.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Change line 484 to `// Sample the incoming Crumbify sheet 50ms after the click, mid-way through the 0.2s`.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: e2e/pile.spec.ts:481 declares `const incoming = page.locator('#sheet-crumbify')`, :483 clicks the 'crumbify' button, and :484's comment says `// Sample "about" 50ms after the click`. No 'about' sheet is involved in this test, so the comment is stale and names the wrong element. It is a documentation accuracy defect, the same class as the fixed code-r5-02 (a wrong header comment).
confirmed.fix: In e2e/pile.spec.ts line 484, replace `// Sample "about" 50ms after the click, mid-way through the 0.2s` with `// Sample the incoming Crumbify sheet 50ms after the click, mid-way through the 0.2s`. Leave line 485 unchanged.

refuted.why: I reproduced the behaviour on out/ served at :5205. Steps: goto '/', wait 400ms, set location.hash='#racing', click the title page, wait 1800ms. Result: the URL is 'http://localhost:5205/' and the title is 'Ali Bars', so the CV is on top. The code path matches the finding: usePile.ts onHashChange queues into pendingRef only when moving !== null, and canBring (pile.ts:112-114) rejects anything while phase !== 'done'. This is not a defect, though. The requirement it cites, docs/acceptance-checklist.md:258 extra-bh-21, says a hashchange brings the matching sheet 'respecting bring() guards', and canBring's first guard is that the intro is done. So ignoring a hash edit during the intro is exactly the behaviour the checklist allows. The replaceState to '/' when the intro ends is useHashSync's documented first-run normalisation (usePile.ts:105-127). It keeps the URL in step with the sheet that is actually on top, so the address bar does not claim #racing while the CV shows. code-r2-02 was a different case: a mid-move Back caused a pushState that truncated forward history and put the pile on the wrong sheet. Here no forward history is lost and the URL is not left out of step with the pile. Queuing hash edits made during the intro would be an enhancement beyond the spec, not a fix.
